items.title: Lily Blanc
items.blurb: A translucent milk base under a glazed top coat, each nail drawn with a single lily in white on white. The quietest set we make.
items.story:
The base goes on in three thin coats rather than one thick one, which is why you can still read the nail underneath it. Anything heavier and the milk turns opaque and dead.

The lily is drawn freehand on each nail with a liner brush, white over white. In a photograph it nearly disappears. In daylight, at arm's length, you catch it and then lose it again.
items.image_alt: A macro photograph of the Lily Blanc set — glazed milk
items.hand_alt: The same hand wearing the Lily Blanc press-on set

items.title: Orchid Veil
items.blurb: Blush pink pressed thin enough to read the nail beneath, with an aurora pearl that pulls lilac in daylight and peach under lamps.
items.story:
The pearl in this one is not a top coat. It is mixed into the blush before anything is applied, so the shift sits inside the colour rather than on top of it and does not wear off the high points first.

One nail on each hand carries an orchid, painted wet-into-wet so the petal edges bleed instead of ending. It is the same technique twice and it never comes out identically.
items.image_alt: A macro photograph of the Orchid Veil set — aurora pearl
items.hand_alt: The same hand wearing the Orchid Veil press-on set

items.title: Matcha Latte
items.blurb: Sage folded into warm cream and left to marble, no two nails alike. Finished satin, so it reads matte until the light catches it.
items.story:
Two colours go on wet and get dragged through each other once. Once is the whole rule — a second pass turns the marble to mud, and there is no way back from it except starting the nail again.

Because the drag is different every time, this is the set where the ten nails least resemble each other. People either want that or they want Lily Blanc.
items.image_alt: A macro photograph of the Matcha Latte set — satin marble
items.hand_alt: The same hand wearing the Matcha Latte press-on set

items.title: Cherry Gloss
items.blurb: Layered translucent red until it holds depth like glass. The gloss is the whole point — it stays wet-looking for the life of the set.
items.story:
Five coats of translucent red, each one cured before the next. A solid red would take one. The difference is that light goes into this and comes back out, so the colour has a floor to it instead of sitting flat on the surface.

The top coat is the thickest we use on any set. It is also why this one photographs badly and looks best in person.
items.image_alt: A macro photograph of the Cherry Gloss set — jelly gloss
items.hand_alt: The same hand wearing the Cherry Gloss press-on set

items.title: Étoile
items.blurb: A mirror chrome that borrows the colour of whatever room you walk into, with crystals set by hand into small four-point stars.
items.story:
Chrome is a powder, not a polish. It is burnished into a cured base with a silicone tip until the surface stops being a coating and starts being a mirror, and any dust under it shows for ever.

The crystals are set one at a time into gel and cured in place rather than glued on afterwards. Glued stones are the ones that leave. These sit slightly below the top coat, which is why the set still feels smooth.
items.image_alt: A macro photograph of the Étoile set — mirror chrome
items.hand_alt: The same hand wearing the Étoile press-on set

items.title: Bunny Cream
items.blurb: A milky nude with a glazed-doughnut sheen, and on two nails a rabbit the size of a grain of rice wearing a blush bow.
items.story:
The glaze is a pearl powder buffed over a warm nude until it goes from cream to something closer to the inside of a shell. It suits most skin tones because there is more beige in it than pink.

The rabbits go on two nails, one per hand. They are about three millimetres tall and they take longer than the other eight nails put together.
items.image_alt: A macro photograph of the Bunny Cream set — glazed pearl
items.hand_alt: The same hand wearing the Bunny Cream press-on set

items.title: Amour
items.blurb: Ten nails on one theme — hearts poured in jelly red, a soda bottle and a love letter built up in relief, and a gingham bow sculpted by hand.
items.story:
Every nail in this set is a different picture, which is the reason it costs what it does and the reason we make very few of them. The bow alone is built in four passes, each one cured before the next so the loops hold their shape instead of slumping.

It is the longest set we offer and the one that suits the fewest people. If you are unsure, it is worth sending us a photograph of your hands first.
